title: The Pitfall of Scaling Up: Uncovering and Mitigating Popularity Bias Amplification in Scaling Transformer-based Recommenders

problem.claim: Scaling transformer-based sequential recommenders improves recommendation accuracy while amplifying popularity bias.

gap.claim: Model scaling creates a sustainability obstacle because increased accuracy is accompanied by amplified popularity bias.

contributions.claim: The authors identify popularity bias amplification as a pitfall of scaling transformer-based sequential recommenders.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that increasing model size improves recommendation accuracy while simultaneously amplifying popularity bias.
The authors report that amplified popularity bias leads systems to over-recommend popular items at the expense of niche items.

narrative_sequence.summary: Scaling model size improves accuracy but amplifies popularity bias.
The amplified bias favors popular items, harms niche items, and undermines fairness and ecosystem diversity.
Bias amplification is presented as a fundamental obstacle to sustainable model scaling.

source_observation.claim: Increasing model capacity can improve accuracy while worsening popularity bias.

interpretation.claim: Scaling should be evaluated across accuracy and distributional effects rather than accuracy alone.

application.claim: Recommendation-system scaling evaluations should include popularity-bias and niche-item outcomes.

exception.claim: The supplied abstract units do not establish whether this tradeoff holds across datasets, architectures, or operating conditions.

unknowns: The mitigation approach and its effectiveness are not specified.
Datasets, baselines, metrics, and experimental conditions are not specified.
